blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines and Australia inked a new defense pact on Sunday, deepening security ties between the two nations that have pushed back against China’s coerciveness in the South China Sea. The Defense Cooperation Agreement (DCA), signed in Manila, updates a 1995 memorandum of understanding and creates what the Philippines and Australia outlined in an August 2026 statement as a “contemporary bilateral defense framework” as the two allies seek to deepen their alliance.
